title: How Changing Ocean Temperatures Could Upend Life on Earth

sentences.zh: 在太空中走过七个十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗星辰之外是什么。

sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》庆祝成立175周年，帮助您理解世界并充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Katrin Benhold.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的卡特琳·本霍尔德。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Many of the effects of climate change are already with us.
sentences.zh: 气候变化的许多影响已经伴随着我们。

sentences.en: Heat waves, droughts, wildfires, flooding.
sentences.zh: 热浪、干旱、野火、洪水。

sentences.en: But some of the most alarming consequences are hiding beneath the surface of the ocean.
sentences.zh: 但一些最令人担忧的后果正隐藏在海洋表面之下。

sentences.en: Today, my colleagues David Gallas and Raymond Zhang on just how close we might be to a tipping point.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事大卫·加拉斯和雷蒙德·张将探讨我们距离临界点究竟有多近。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, May 7th.
sentences.zh: 今天是5月7日，星期二。

sentences.en: David, you've been writing about different aspects of climate change for years and are definitely no stranger to distressing news about a warming planet.
sentences.zh: 大卫，你多年来一直在撰写关于气候变化各个方面的文章，对关于地球变暖的令人不安的消息肯定不陌生。

sentences.en: But something about ocean temperatures seems particularly distressing.
sentences.zh: 但海洋温度的某些变化似乎格外令人担忧。

sentences.en: What's going on?
sentences.zh: 发生了什么？

sentences.en: Starting last year, scientists started noting something alarming happening in oceans all around the world.
sentences.zh: 从去年开始，科学家们开始注意到世界各地海洋中发生的一件令人担忧的事情。

sentences.en: It was warm in the oceans, but it started to get really hot in ways that they had never seen before.
sentences.zh: 海洋原本就很温暖，但它开始以他们从未见过的方式变得异常炎热。

sentences.en: And for the last year plus, I've been checking in with scientists, and they are increasingly concerned, perplexed even, with what they're seeing.
sentences.zh: 在过去的一年多里，我一直在与科学家们沟通，他们对所看到的情况越来越担忧，甚至感到困惑。

sentences.en: And when you say oceans are getting hotter, can you just give me a sense of how much the oceans are warming and how fast?
sentences.zh: 当你大卫说海洋正在变热时，你能让我大概了解一下海洋变暖了多少，速度有多快吗？

sentences.en: Well, if you look at a chart that shows, say, the last two or three decades of average sea surface temperatures, you'll see a gradual warming trend.
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果你看一张显示最近两到三十年平均海面温度的图表，你会看到一个逐渐变暖的趋势。

sentences.en: But starting last March, we didn't see another gradual increase.
sentences.zh: 但从去年3月开始，我们看到的不再是逐渐上升。

sentences.en: We saw this big jump.
sentences.zh: 我们看到了这个巨大的跃升。

sentences.en: And from March of 2023 on, it stayed hot, and it's just getting hotter.
sentences.zh: 从2023年3月开始，它一直保持高温，而且还在变得更热。

sentences.en: And we began 2024 at this much higher level than we've ever seen before, and we're still there.
sentences.zh: 我们以远高于以往的水平开始了2024年，而且我们依然停留在那里。

sentences.en: And in many parts of the world, the temperatures are still going up as we head into summer.
sentences.zh: 在世界许多地方，随着我们进入夏季，温度仍在继续上升。

sentences.en: And that has scientists really concerned.
sentences.zh: 这让科学家们非常担忧。

sentences.en: And you said earlier that none of the scientists that you've been checking in with, and none of these very sophisticated climate models that they're operating with,
sentences.zh: 你之前说过，你联系过的所有科学家，以及他们运行的所有这些高度复杂的气候模型，

sentences.en: can explain this big jump.
sentences.zh: 都无法解释这个巨大的跃升。

sentences.en: And I guess I have to ask at this point, why are these scientists so surprised?
sentences.zh: 我想我不得不在这时问一句，为什么这些科学家会如此惊讶？

sentences.en: I mean, we've seen record-breaking heatwaves for the past several years.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，过去几年我们已经见证了打破纪录的热浪。

sentences.en: It seems like every single year is hotter than the laSt.
sentences.zh: 似乎每一年都比前一年更热。

sentences.en: Why is it any surprise that the ocean is no different?
sentences.zh: 为什么海洋没有什么不同会让人感到惊讶？

sentences.en: Well, they're not surprised that the ocean's warming.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们对海洋变暖并不感到惊讶。

sentences.en: They have understood for many years now that the overall man-made global warming that we're experiencing all over the world in all these different ways
sentences.zh: 多年来，他们一直明白，我们在世界各地以各种不同方式正在经历的整体人为全球变暖，

sentences.en: is going to affect the oceans.
sentences.zh: 将会影响海洋。

sentences.en: Water is very absorbent for heat, and a lot of the extra heat that we're producing from the burning of fossil fuels, a lot of the extra heat that's being caused in the atmosphere
sentences.zh: 水对热有很强的吸收能力，我们因燃烧化石燃料而产生的大量额外热量，以及大气中因此产生的大量额外热量，

sentences.en: as a result of that, is just getting sucked into the ocean.
sentences.zh: 都被吸入了海洋中。

sentences.en: And bit by bit over the last many decades, the oceans have gotten warmer.
sentences.zh: 在过去的几十年里，海洋一点一点地变得更暖。

sentences.en: So even after the air cools, say in winter or something, the ocean holds on to a portion of that heat.
sentences.zh: 所以即使在空气冷却之后，比如在冬天左右，海洋仍然保留了一部分热量。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没通过。

sentences.en: Even when it's cold outside, the oceans, year after year, have been getting a little warmer as a result of climate change.
sentences.zh: 即使外面很冷，由于气候变化，海洋年复一年地变得越来越暖。

sentences.en: But that on its own does not account for the kind of warming that we're seeing right now.
sentences.zh: 但仅凭这一点，并不能解释我们现在看到的这种变暖现象。

sentences.en: Not even close.
sentences.zh: 差得远呢。

sentences.en: So what else do they think could be going on?
sentences.zh: 那么他们认为还可能发生了什么？

sentences.en: Well, for the last year or so, the Pacific Ocean has been going through an El Nino cycle, which is when a lot of excess heat is released from the ocean.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在过去一年左右的时间里，太平洋一直在经历厄尔尼诺周期，也就是海洋释放大量多余热量的时期。

sentences.en: And in addition to making the Pacific ocean hotter, it has sort of an overall warming nudge, a little boost for warmth in ocean heat around the world.
sentences.zh: 除了让太平洋变得更热之外，它还在全球海洋热量方面产生了一种整体变暖的推动作用，带来了一点微小的提升。

sentences.en: But even that doesn't explain the big jumps we've seen.
sentences.zh: 但即使是这样也无法解释我们所看到的巨大跃升。

sentences.en: And there's another counterintuitive factor that scientists believe is playing a role here as well.
sentences.zh: 还有一个反直觉的因素，科学家认为它在这里也发挥了一定作用。

sentences.en: And that has everything to do with the pollution being emitted by big ocean liners, by big ships traveling across the Atlantic.
sentences.zh: 这与大型远洋客轮和横跨大西洋的大型船舶排放的污染密切相关。

sentences.en: So in 2020, some shipping regulations changed.
sentences.zh: 所以在2020年，一些航运法规发生了变化。

sentences.en: And they required that the emissions from the fuel being used in big ocean tankers become much cleaner.
sentences.zh: 它们要求大型远洋油轮所用燃料的排放物变得更加清洁。

sentences.en: And as a result of that, there was less sulfur dioxide in the shipping emissions.
sentences.zh: 因此，航运排放物中的二氧化硫减少了。

sentences.en: That's a good thing for many reasons.
sentences.zh: 出于多种原因，这是一件好事。

sentences.en: Sulfur dioxide is a pollutant.
sentences.zh: 二氧化硫是一种污染物。

sentences.en: It can have really adverse health effects on humans.
sentences.zh: 它会对人类健康产生非常不利的影响。

sentences.en: But one of the things it was also doing was refracting sunlight away from the oceans.
sentences.zh: 但它的另一个作用是将阳光从海洋反射开去。

sentences.en: And so what we've seen over the last recent years is as there was less sulfur dioxide in the North Atlantic, as less and less of that particulate matter was in the atmosphere
sentences.zh: 因此我们在近年来看到的是，随着北大西洋中的二氧化硫减少，随着大气中这种颗粒物越来越少，

sentences.en: and able to bounce the sun's energy back into space.
sentences.zh: 并且能够将太阳的能量反射回太空。

sentences.en: More and more of the sun's energy, more and more of the sun's heat, was making its way into the oceans.
sentences.zh: 越来越多的太阳能量，越来越多的太阳热量，进入了海洋。

sentences.en: And that, scientists are now understanding, likely played a warming role as well.
sentences.zh: 科学家现在了解到，这可能也起到了让海水变暖的作用。

sentences.en: So basically, lower emissions in these shipping lanes means less kind of smoggy cloud cover, and therefore more direct sunlight hitting the ocean's surface and heating it up.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，这些航运路线上的排放减少意味着某种烟雾状云层减少，因此更多的阳光直接照射到海洋表面并使其变暖。

sentences.en: Which actually kind of rings a bell, because we talked about this in the show recently,
sentences.zh: 这其实听起来有点耳熟，因为我们在节目中最近讨论过这一点，

sentences.en: in relation to scientists wanting to artificially create more potent cloud cover to cool down the planet.
sentences.zh: 这与科学家想要人工制造更强效的云层来冷却地球有关。

sentences.en: It's a little ironic that scientists are now trying to engineer the very thing we were trying to stop doing.
sentences.zh: 有点讽刺的是，科学家现在正试图设计我们一直试图停止做的事情。

sentences.en: Talk about unintended consequences.
sentences.zh: 这就是所谓的意料之外的后果。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And this is one of those instances where there are these very tough trade-offs, right?
sentences.zh: 这也是其中一个例子，存在着非常艰难的权衡，对吧？

sentences.en: It's great, yes, that we have less pollution.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们的污染减少了，这很好。

sentences.en: That's going to be good for public health.
sentences.zh: 这对公众健康有好处。

sentences.en: On the other hand, it may have allowed yet more warming in the oceans that's having cascading effects across all sorts of ecosystems that we're only just beginning to understand.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，它可能导致海洋进一步变暖，从而对各种生态系统产生连锁反应，而我们才刚刚开始了解这些影响。

sentences.en: Yeah, let's talk about that for a moment.
sentences.zh: 是的，让我们讨论一下这个。

sentences.en: What are the effects of this mysterious warming?
sentences.zh: 这种神秘变暖的影响是什么？

sentences.en: You mentioned ecosysteMs.
sentences.zh: 你提到了生态系统。

sentences.en: Well, there are a lot of effects when the oceans get this hot this faSt.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当海洋变得如此炎热且速度如此之快时，会有很多影响。

sentences.en: But perhaps the most immediate concern among people all over the world is the fact that in dozens and dozens of countries all over the world,
sentences.zh: 但也许全世界人们最直接关心的是这样一个事实：在世界几十个国家中，

sentences.en: we're experiencing a record wave of coral bleaching.
sentences.zh: 我们正在经历创纪录的珊瑚白化浪潮。

sentences.en: Which is to say that coral reefs, these vitally important parts of the ocean ecosystems, are just dying at a rate we've never really seen before.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，珊瑚礁这些海洋生态系统中至关重要的部分，正以我们从未见过的速度消亡。

sentences.en: And that's going to have all sorts of negative effects for fisheries all over the globe.
sentences.zh: 这将对全球各地的渔业产生各种负面影响。

sentences.en: Why are coral reefs so important?
sentences.zh: 为什么珊瑚礁如此重要？

sentences.en: Well, they matter for a lot more than just snorkeling.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它们的重要性远远不止于浮潜。

sentences.en: Yes, they're beautiful.
sentences.zh: 是的，它们很美。

sentences.en: And yes, they are the center of a lot of tourist activity.
sentences.zh: 是的，它们是许多旅游活动的中心。

sentences.en: But they're also sort of this fundamental foundational part of the marine food chain.
sentences.zh: 但它们也是海洋食物链中一种基础性的核心部分。

sentences.en: And so when we think about all of the life that coral reefs sustain, that all allows for smaller fish to flourish and go out into the ocean.
sentences.zh: 因此，当我们想到珊瑚礁维持的所有生命时，这一切都使得小鱼能够繁衍生息并进入海洋。

sentences.en: And those smaller fish contribute to the lives and the ecosystems of bigger fish.
sentences.zh: 而那些小鱼为大鱼的生活和生态系统做出了贡献。

sentences.en: And when we think back to, you know, the food chain that we learned about when we were in elementary school, coral reefs are right at the bottom of that.
sentences.zh: 当我们回想起我们在小学学到的食物链时，珊瑚礁就处于最底层。

sentences.en: And if we lose that, it's going to have devastating effects for marine ecosystems all over the world.
sentences.zh: 如果我们失去了它，将对全世界的海洋生态系统产生毁灭性的影响。

sentences.en: Is there any hope to save the coral at this point or are they doomed?
sentences.zh: 目前还有希望拯救珊瑚吗，还是它们已经注定消亡了？

sentences.en: My colleague Katrin Einhorn has been doing a lot of great reporting on the situation with corals and she's highlighted some of the efforts
sentences.zh: 我的同事卡特琳·艾恩霍恩一直在对珊瑚的状况进行大量出色的报道，她强调了一些正在进行的旨在拯救它们的努力，以培育出更有韧性的珊瑚。

sentences.en: underway to try to save them, to grow more resilient corals.
sentences.zh: 但事实是，我们看到的大规模白化事件发生在世界各地的56个左右的国家，

sentences.en: But the truth is the scale we're seeing with bleaching events happening all around the world in something like 56 countries,
sentences.zh: 目前根本不可能完全阻止它。

sentences.en: it's just not possible to stop it entirely at this point.
sentences.zh: 所以它是我们生态系统中的多米诺骨牌之一，可能会引发一系列问题，并实际上导致重大损失。

sentences.en: So it's one of these dominoes in our ecosystem that can set up a whole range of problems and actually result in major losses.
sentences.zh: 回到这一切的神秘之处，当这些多米诺骨牌开始倒下时，我们根本不知道会发生什么。

sentences.en: And just to come back to the mystery of it all, we just don't know what happens when those dominoes start to fall.
sentences.zh: 受到影响的不仅仅是珊瑚。

sentences.en: And it's not just corals that are being impacted here.
sentences.zh: 由于海洋变暖，天气也很可能会发生变化。

sentences.en: The weather could well change as a result of these warmer oceans as well.
sentences.zh: 我特别想到的是即将到来的大西洋飓风季。

sentences.en: And I'm particularly thinking about the upcoming Atlantic hurricane season.
sentences.zh: 温暖的海水是飓风的关键要素。

sentences.en: Warm water is a key ingredient to hurricanes.
sentences.zh: 当你想到飓风以及它们的强度和增强速度时，这两个动力学中最重要的因素之一就是水温有多高。

sentences.en: When you think about hurricanes and how strong they get and how fast they intensify, one of the most important factors in both of those dynamics is how hot the water is.
sentences.zh: 当我们看到所有这些温暖的海水聚集在大西洋时，这导致气象预报员预测北大西洋即将迎来一个可能打破纪录的飓风季。

sentences.en: And when we see all this warm water hanging out in the Atlantic Ocean, that is leading forecasters to predict a potentially record-breaking hurricane season
sentences.zh: 这可能会影响加勒比地区、北美及其他地区。

sentences.en: that is right around the corner in the North Atlantic.
sentences.zh: 让我感到震惊的是，我们知道海洋正在变得热得多。

sentences.en: And that could affect the Caribbean, North America, and beyond.
sentences.zh: 我们并不完全知道原因。

sentences.en: What's striking to me is that, you know, we know that the oceans are getting much hotter.
sentences.zh: 我们也无法完全解释其影响会是什么，这听起来确实不太妙。

sentences.en: We don't fully know why.
sentences.zh: 但如果我们不完全了解发生了什么，我们又怎么能指望对此做点什么呢？

sentences.en: And we can't fully explain what the impact will be, which really doesn't sound great.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我一直在问科学家这个问题，对吧？

sentences.en: But if we don't fully understand what's going on, then how can we even hope to do something about it?
sentences.zh: 比如，有什么可以做的？

sentences.en: Well, I've been asking scientists this very question, right?
sentences.zh: 艰难的答案是，没有简单的方法来调低海洋的恒温器。

sentences.en: Like, what is there to be done?
sentences.zh: 这种变暖正在发生，我们现在的任务是尽最大努力与之共存。

sentences.en: And the tough answer is there's no easy way to turn down the thermostat of the oceans.
sentences.zh: 我们甚至还没有谈到有些人认为的最大威胁。

sentences.en: This warming is happening, and our job now is to live with it as best we can.
sentences.zh: 随着海洋变暖，它们正在助长冰川融化和北极海冰的流失。

sentences.en: And we haven't even talked about what some people regard as the biggest threat of all.
sentences.zh: 随着这种情况的发生，许多人不仅担心海平面上升，还担心对一个至关重要的海洋洋流的破坏。

sentences.en: As the oceans warm, they're contributing to the melting of glaciers and the loss of Arctic sea ice.
sentences.zh: 如果发生这种情况，可能会对整个星球产生巨大的影响。

sentences.en: And as that happens, many people are worried not just about rising sea levels, but also about the disruption to a vitally important ocean current.
sentences.zh: 它几乎可以改变我们所知的地球生命的一切。

sentences.en: And if that happens, it could have massive ramifications for the entire planet.
sentences.zh: 休息过后，我的同事雷蒙德·宗将讨论该洋流崩溃的可能性。

sentences.en: It could change just about everything we know about life on Earth.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: After the break, my colleague Raymond Jong talks about the possibility of that ocean current collapsing.
sentences.zh: 我是韦娜·刘。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我编写《纽约时报》游戏中的拼图游戏之一“连连看”（Connections）。

sentences.en: I'm Wena Liu.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢试图捉弄你。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖斯基，我每天都创作“拼字蜜蜂”（Spelling Bee）和“字母盒”（Letterboxd）游戏。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我有种叫做联觉的东西。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 当我听音乐时我能看到颜色。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由真人制作的，就像你刚刚听到那些人一样。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com slash games 开始今天的游戏。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 雷蒙德，在休息之前，我们的同事大卫·加勒斯向我们讲述了海洋变暖的这一惊人趋势以及由此产生的一些非常令人担忧的后果。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 但你来到这里是要告诉我们海洋中可能正在发生的其他事情，与洋流有关的事情。

sentences.en: Raymond, before the break, our colleague David Gallus told us all about this alarming trend of the ocean heating up and some of the very worrying consequences of that.
sentences.zh: 说实话，这听起来像是科幻电影里的情节。

sentences.en: But you are here to tell us about something else that may be happening in the ocean, something to do with ocean currents.
sentences.zh: 你能解释一下吗？

sentences.en: And if I'm honest, it sounds like something straight out of a science fiction movie.
sentences.zh: 当然可以，卡特琳。

sentences.en: Can you explain?
sentences.zh: 其实你说得对。

sentences.en: Sure, Katrin.
sentences.zh: 这确实是科幻电影里的情节。

sentences.en: And actually, you're right.
sentences.zh: 我现在在新德里的全球变暖会议上，如果你敢相信自己的眼睛，这里正在下雪。

sentences.en: It is something from a science fiction movie.
sentences.zh: 大约20年前，一部名为《后天》的电影上映了。

sentences.en: I'm here at the Global Warming Conference in New Delhi, where if you can believe your eyes, it's snowing.
sentences.zh: 唯一有足够力量影响全球天气的力量是太阳。

sentences.en: About 20 years ago, a movie called The Day After Tomorrow came out.
sentences.zh: 北大西洋洋流呢？

sentences.en: The only force strong enough to affect global weather is the sun.
sentences.zh: 我昨晚接到海德隆中心拉普森教授的电话。

sentences.en: What about the North Atlantic current?
sentences.zh: 他认为洋流已经改变了。

sentences.en: I got a call last night from Professor Rapson at the Hedlund Center.
sentences.zh: 哦，得了吧，杰克。

sentences.en: He thinks the current has changed.
sentences.zh: 我不认识你。

sentences.en: Oh, come on, Jack.
sentences.zh: 我不知道你在说什么。

sentences.en: How could that be?
sentences.zh: 怎么会这样？

sentences.en: And the plot of that movie is that there's this major ocean current in the Atlantic that suddenly stops moving.
sentences.zh: 那部电影的情节是大西洋中有一股巨大的洋流突然停止了流动。

sentences.en: It collapses.
sentences.zh: 它崩溃了。

sentences.en: And it sets off this cascade of natural disasters.
sentences.zh: 并引发了一连串的自然灾害。

sentences.en: In Nova Scotia earlier today, the ocean rose by 25 feet in a matter of seconds.
sentences.zh: 今天早些时候在新斯科舍省，海洋在几秒钟内上升了25英尺。

sentences.en: What you're seeing are two actual tornadoes striking Los Angeles International Airport.
sentences.zh: 你现在看到的是两场真正的龙卷风袭击洛杉矶国际机场。

sentences.en: It's a mob scene here at Grand Central Station.
sentences.zh: 中央车站这里现在乱成了一团。

sentences.en: Over half the platforms are flooded and service has been suspended on all trains.
sentences.zh: 超过一半的站台被淹，所有列车的服务都已暂停。

sentences.en: That ultimately plunged the planet into a new ice age.
sentences.zh: 这最终让地球陷入了新冰河时代。

sentences.en: What can we do?
sentences.zh: 我们能做什么？

sentences.en: Save as many as you can.
sentences.zh: 能救多少就救多少。

sentences.en: I guess my question to you, Raymond, given what we're talking about here, is which part of that movie is science fiction and which part is actual science?
sentences.zh: 我想问你的是，雷蒙德，鉴于我们今天讨论的内容，那部电影里哪部分是科幻，哪部分是真正的科学？

sentences.en: I'd say most of the movie is pretty purely fiction.
sentences.zh: 我会说这部电影大部分都纯属虚构。

sentences.en: But there is a kernel of truth in the science, which is that this vital ocean current in the Atlantic is very real.
sentences.zh: 但科学中确实包含一丝真相，那就是大西洋中这个至关重要的洋流是真实存在的。

sentences.en: And just like in the movie, scientists are worried about what happens if it shuts down.
sentences.zh: 就像电影里一样，科学家们很担心如果它停转会发生什么。

sentences.en: Okay, so tell me about this current.
sentences.zh: 好的，跟我讲讲这个洋流吧。

sentences.en: Scientists have given it a very, very unwieldy name.
sentences.zh: 科学家们给它起了一个非常非常拗口的名字。

sentences.en: They call it the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation.
sentences.zh: 他们称之为大西洋经向翻转环流。

sentences.en: But most people just use the acronym AMOC.
sentences.zh: 但大多数人只用它的缩写 AMOC。

sentences.en: AMOC.
sentences.zh: AMOC。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Think of it as a giant conveyor belt of water that loops around the Atlantic Ocean.
sentences.zh: 把它想象成一条贯穿大西洋的巨型水流传送带。

sentences.en: And it starts near the equator, goes up through the Caribbean, around the east coast of the U.S., up toward northern Europe, and then back again.
sentences.zh: 它发源于赤道附近，向北穿过加勒比海，绕过美国东海岸，朝北欧前进，然后再折返。

sentences.en: Scientists have come to realize how important AMOC is for a lot of the climate that we enjoy today.
sentences.zh: 科学家们已经意识到，对于我们今天享有的大部分气候而言，AMOC 是多么重要。

sentences.en: A lot of northern Europe,
sentences.zh: 北欧的大部分地区，

sentences.en: Britain, Iceland, Scandinavia, is habitable today, really, because of AMOC.
sentences.zh: 英国、冰岛、斯堪的纳维亚，如今之所以适宜居住，实际上正是因为 AMOC。

sentences.en: It's because this system transports heat from the equator and very generously drops it off in northern Europe that even though it's so far from the equator,
sentences.zh: 正是因为这个系统将赤道的热量输送过来，并慷慨地释放在北欧，所以尽管它距离赤道那么远，

sentences.en: it's not as uninhabitable as, say, far northern Canada or Siberia.
sentences.zh: 它也不会像比如加拿大北部或西伯利亚那样不宜居。

sentences.en: And let me just ask you, is this AMOC current the same thing as the Gulf Stream, which people write about and are worried about a lot these days?
sentences.zh: 我想问一下，这个 AMOC 洋流和人们近来经常撰文并担忧的墨西哥湾流是同一回事吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, the Gulf Stream is a similar system of currents, but AMOC is sort of the full loop.
sentences.zh: 对，墨西哥湾流是一个类似的洋流系统，但 AMOC 可以说是一个完整的循环。

sentences.en: The Gulf Stream is just one part of it, but AMOC is really what's important for the climate.
sentences.zh: 墨西哥湾流只是其中的一部分，而 AMOC 才是对气候真正至关重要的东西。

sentences.en: Okay, so before we talk about
sentences.zh: 好的，所以在我们讨论

sentences.en: AMOC shutting down or collapsing, can you actually kind of give me a quick science 101 explanation of how this thing works?
sentences.zh: AMOC 停转或崩溃之前，你能先做一个简单的科学入门解释，说明这东西是如何运作的吗？

sentences.en: Like, there's this massive loop of water, like a sort of, I guess, an underwater river that you described, which kind of transports warm water up towards the north
sentences.zh: 比如，有这样一股巨大的水流循环，就像你描述的那种水下河流，它把温水输送到北方，

sentences.en: and then comes back as cold water.
sentences.zh: 然后作为冷水返回。

sentences.en: What keeps this thing running?
sentences.zh: 是什么让这个系统持续运转的？

sentences.en: How does a current just stay in constant motion and loop around like that?
sentences.zh: 一股洋流怎么能保持恒定的运动并这样循环呢？

sentences.en: It has to do primarily with differences in temperature and salinity.
sentences.zh: 这主要与温度和盐度的差异有关。

sentences.en: Basically, fluids want to keep moving in a particular direction.
sentences.zh: 基本上，流体倾向于朝着特定的方向持续流动。

sentences.en: And it's driven by this balance between warm water, cold water, salty water, fresh water.
sentences.zh: 它是由暖水、冷水、咸水和淡水之间的这种平衡驱动的。

sentences.en: Heavier water wants to sink.
sentences.zh: 较重的水会下沉。

sentences.en: Lighter water wants to rise.
sentences.zh: 较轻的水会上浮。

sentences.en: And so the temperature and salinity of the water is sort of what determines how dense it is.
sentences.zh: 因此，水的温度和盐度在某种程度上决定了它的密度。

sentences.en: And this density and differences in density keeps this giant loop moving.
sentences.zh: 正是这种密度以及密度的差异，让这个巨大的循环不断运动。

sentences.en: It's something that explorers noted in the Atlantic hundreds of years ago.
sentences.zh: 这是几百年前大西洋探险家们就注意到的一种现象。

sentences.en: They noticed that deep water was very cold.
sentences.zh: 他们发现深层海水非常冷。

sentences.en: It was unexpected.
sentences.zh: 这出乎意料。

sentences.en: And so I think as people have started studying the oceans more and science has advanced, they've realized there's a very delicate system of differences in temperature and salinity
sentences.zh: 所以我想，随着人们对海洋的研究不断深入以及科学的进步，他们意识到正是这种极其微妙的温度和盐度差异系统，

sentences.en: that keeps this conveyor belt moving.
sentences.zh: 才让这条传送带不断运转。

sentences.en: That's really fascinating.
sentences.zh: 这太迷人了。

sentences.en: I mean, I've always known we had these currents and that they were really important, but I never really appreciated and understood what it takes to keep them going.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我一直都知道有这些洋流，而且它们非常重要，但我从未真正体会和理解维持它们运转需要什么条件。

sentences.en: So, okay, tell me why scientists are so worried about AMOC shutting down.
sentences.zh: 好吧，告诉我为什么科学家们如此担心 AMOC 停转。

sentences.en: As the planet warms, there's something that might be significantly affecting this delicate balance.
sentences.zh: 随着地球变暖，某种因素可能会严重影响这种微妙的平衡。

sentences.en: And that's the melting of the Greenland ice sheet.
sentences.zh: 那就是格陵兰冰盖的融化。

sentences.en: With the melting of the ice, there's this big infusion of fresh water into the Northern Atlantic.
sentences.zh: 随着冰层融化，大量淡水注入北大西洋。

sentences.en: And because that affects the salinity of the Northern Atlantic, it sort of changes the balance of salinity and temperature, potentially enough to knock this loop off course.
sentences.zh: 由于这影响了北大西洋的盐度，它在某种程度上改变了盐度和温度的平衡，其影响程度可能足以让这个循环偏离轨道。

sentences.en: And there's signs already that this is happening, that at least the current is slowing down.
sentences.zh: 并且已经有迹象表明这种情况正在发生，至少洋流正在减缓。

sentences.en: And one major piece of evidence is this cold blob that's appeared in the Northern Atlantic.
sentences.zh: 一个主要的证据就是北大西洋出现的这个冷水团。

sentences.en: A cold blob.
sentences.zh: 一个冷水团。

sentences.en: A cold blob, that's right.
sentences.zh: 一个冷水团，没错。

sentences.en: With most, almost everywhere on the planet getting warmer because of the greenhouse gases that we're putting into the atmosphere, there's a conspicuous blob
sentences.zh: 由于我们排放到大气中的温室气体，地球上几乎每个地方都在变暖，但在格陵兰岛附近的北大西洋，

sentences.en: in the North Atlantic near Greenland that is getting cooler.
sentences.zh: 有一个显眼的冷水团却在变冷。

sentences.en: And it's exactly the place that scientists would expect to be getting cooler if AMOC were slowing down.
sentences.zh: 这正是科学家们预期如果 AMOC 减缓时会变冷的区域。

sentences.en: Okay, so the Greenland ice sheet is melting due to climate change.
sentences.zh: 好的，所以格陵兰冰盖由于气候变化正在融化。

sentences.en: And that seems to be disrupting this current.
sentences.zh: 这似乎正在扰乱这个洋流。

sentences.en: So as a result, less warm water is being transported north.
sentences.zh: 因此，输送到北方的温水减少了。

sentences.en: And that's why we have this cold blob that scientists have noticed in the North Atlantic.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么科学家们在北大西洋注意到了这个冷水团。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And do we know what would happen if the current collapsed today?
sentences.zh: 我们知道如果洋流今天崩溃会发生什么吗？

sentences.en: So the best source of information we have about what happens when AMOC collapses comes from about 12,800 years ago,
sentences.zh: 我们拥有的关于 AMOC 崩溃后果的最佳信息来源大约来自 12,800 年前，

sentences.en: which is, as far as scientists know, the last major time this happened.
sentences.zh: 就科学家所知，那是上一次发生这种重大事件的时期。

sentences.en: Basically, the climate changed really, really quickly, at least by geological time.
sentences.zh: 基本上，气候变化得非常非常快，至少以地质时间尺度来看是这样。

sentences.en: It was sort of less than 100 years, as far as scientists know.
sentences.zh: 据科学家所知，时间甚至不到 100 年。

sentences.en: Much of the Northern Hemisphere got cold again.
sentences.zh: 北半球的大部分地区再次变冷。

sentences.en: The temperature in parts of Greenland probably fell by about 18 degrees Fahrenheit.
sentences.zh: 格陵兰部分地区的温度可能下降了大约 18 华氏度。

sentences.en: Forests were replaced by tundra.
sentences.zh: 森林被苔原取代。

sentences.en: Ice sheets grew again.
sentences.zh: 冰盖再次生长。

sentences.en: As far away as California and the southwestern U.S., you had evidence of cooler, drier conditions.
sentences.zh: 远至加利福尼亚和美国西南部，都有出现更冷、更干燥环境的迹象。

sentences.en: And as far as scientists can tell, this may even have contributed to the disappearance of some of our early hunter-gatherer civilizations.
sentences.zh: 据科学家所知，这甚至可能导致了我们某些早期猎人采集文明的消失。

sentences.en: Some of our ancestors were probably pushing into new territory as the ice sheets retreated and were suddenly confronted with another blast of cold.
sentences.zh: 随着冰盖退缩，我们的一些祖先可能正在向新领地推进，却突然遭遇了又一次寒潮的打击。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So the last time this happened, this current shutdown, the world was basically plunged into an ice age and wiped out part of humanity.
sentences.zh: 所以上一次发生这种情况、洋流停转时，世界基本上陷入了冰河时代，并毁灭了一部分人类。

sentences.en: Is that the scenario we're looking at today?
sentences.zh: 这就是我们今天面临的情景吗？

sentences.en: I think scientists are careful about not being too precise about what it would look like if it happened again.
sentences.zh: 我认为科学家们在预测如果再次发生会是什么样时非常谨慎，避免过于绝对。

sentences.en: The world, after all, is still warming.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，世界仍在变暖。

sentences.en: And so in a lot of ways, the climate is already quite different from the one that was around at the time.
sentences.zh: 因此在许多方面，当前的气候已经与那个时期的气候大不相同。

sentences.en: But certainly, I think scientists expect
sentences.zh: 但可以肯定的是，科学家们确实预计

sentences.en: Northern Europe, the U.K.,
sentences.zh: 北欧、英国、

sentences.en: Iceland,
sentences.zh: 冰岛、

sentences.en: Scandinavia, to become a much colder place even than it was
sentences.zh: 斯堪的纳维亚，会变得比

sentences.en: 200 years ago before the Industrial Revolution, before humans started adding greenhouse gases to the atmosphere.
sentences.zh: 200 年前工业革命之前、人类开始向大气中增加温室气体之前还要寒冷得多。

sentences.en: How cold are we talking?
sentences.zh: 我们说的是有多冷？

sentences.en: You mentioned the U.K.
sentences.zh: 你提到了英国。

sentences.en: I'm in the U.K.
sentences.zh: 我现在就

sentences.en: right now.
sentences.zh: 在英国。

sentences.en: I mean, would Britain suddenly look like the frozen tundra?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，英国会突然变成冰冻的苔原吗？

sentences.en: It would be significantly colder.
sentences.zh: 它会显著变冷。

sentences.en: It's far north enough to really be almost Arctic.
sentences.zh: 它的纬度已经足够高，几乎要接近北极了。

sentences.en: And I think an AMOC collapse could bring much stronger winter storms, deep cold in the winter that would be extremely dangerous.
sentences.zh: 我认为 AMOC 崩溃可能会带来更强烈的冬季风暴，以及极其危险的严冬。

sentences.en: But at the same time, that cold around the North Atlantic doesn't just translate straightforwardly into cold everywhere.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，北大西洋周围的寒冷并不意味着到处都会直接变冷。

sentences.en: Basically, if you don't have AMOC, you have more heat that stays around the tropics and the equator.
sentences.zh: 基本上，如果没有了 AMOC，就会有更多热量滞留在热带和赤道附近。

sentences.en: A warm ocean around the equator gives the fuel to storms around the equator and rainfall around the equator.
sentences.zh: 赤道周围温暖的海洋为赤道周围的风暴和降雨提供了能量。

sentences.en: So it's not just about getting that warm water from the tropics to Europe, it's also getting that warm water away from the tropics to avoid things like extreme weather events.
sentences.zh: 所以这不仅关乎将热带的温水输送到欧洲，也关乎将温水从热带带走，以避免极端天气事件等情况发生。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And it's not just about the temperatures people would experience.
sentences.zh: 这不仅关乎人们将经历的温度。

sentences.en: It's also about agriculture.
sentences.zh: 这也关乎农业。

sentences.en: And especially in vulnerable places like Africa,
sentences.zh: 特别是在非洲等脆弱地区，

sentences.en: big shifts in rainfall, big shifts in temperature could really affect food chains, food supplies, our ability to feed ourselves.
sentences.zh: 降雨的大幅变化、温度的大幅变化可能会真正影响食物链、粮食供应以及我们养活自己的能力。

sentences.en: And what does that mean for humans living in these places?
sentences.zh: 这对于生活在这些地方的人类意味着什么？

sentences.en: Like, you were saying that 13,000 years ago,
sentences.zh: 比如，你刚才说 13,000 年前，

sentences.en: Northern Europe basically wasn't inhabitable anymore.
sentences.zh: 北欧基本上已经不再适宜人类居住。

sentences.en: Would humans still be able to live in these places?
sentences.zh: 人类还能在这些地方生存吗？

sentences.en: We, as a civilization, as a species, obviously have some ability to withstand a range of temperatures, a range of weather conditions.
sentences.zh: 作为一种文明、一个物种，我们显然具备一定的承受各种温度、各种天气条件的能力。

sentences.en: But we really haven't seen, in our recent history at least, changes as fast as the ones scientists imagine an AMOC collapse would bring.
sentences.zh: 但至少在我们的近代史上，我们从未见过科学家们所设想的 AMOC 崩溃所带来的如此迅速的变化。

sentences.en: It's really hard to say is Northern Europe ready for a much colder climate than it is right now.
sentences.zh: 很难说北欧是否已经准备好迎接比现在冷得多的气候。

sentences.en: If, for instance, sea level rise accelerates on the east coast of the U.S., are cities there prepared?
sentences.zh: 例如，如果美国东海岸的海平面上升加速，那里的城市准备好了吗？

sentences.en: That's another consequence of AMOC that scientists are worried about.
sentences.zh: 这是科学家们担心的 AMOC 的另一个后果。

sentences.en: And it's obviously already happening, and you can see the effects of sea level rise in places like the Gulf Coast,
sentences.zh: 这显然已经在发生了，你可以在墨西哥湾沿岸、

sentences.en: North Carolina,
sentences.zh: 北卡罗来纳州、

sentences.en: Florida, even New York.
sentences.zh: 佛罗里达甚至纽约等地看到海平面上升的影响。

sentences.en: But certainly it would be a test for countries, societies, around the Northern
sentences.zh: 但可以肯定的是，这将是对北大西洋周边国家和

sentences.en: Atlantic that they haven't seen before.
sentences.zh: 社会前所未有的考验。

sentences.en: Okay, that's a very scary prospect with everything that goes with it.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这是一个非常可怕的前景，伴随着所有相关的后果。

sentences.en: You know, mass floods and displacement of people, climate migration, everything that you can sort of imagine.
sentences.zh: 你知道，大规模洪水、人口流离失所、气候难民，以及你能想象到的一切。

sentences.en: When do scientists predict that this could actually happen based on the data they have and assuming, of course, current human behavior and emissions don't change?
sentences.zh: 根据他们掌握的数据，并假设人类当前的行为和排放保持不变，科学家预测这可能在什么时候实际发生？

sentences.en: As best as scientists can tell right now, they know
sentences.zh: 据科学家目前所知，他们知道

sentences.en: AMOC is weakening.
sentences.zh: AMOC 正在减弱。

sentences.en: They expect it to continue weakening.
sentences.zh: 他们预计它会继续减弱。

sentences.en: Whether a collapse is imminent, whether it's far away, is still really, really hard to say.
sentences.zh: 崩溃是否迫在眉睫，还是遥不可期，目前依然很难说。

sentences.en: But it couldn't quickly be reversed.
sentences.zh: 但它无法迅速逆转。

sentences.en: Once you sort of started on this process, the system just keeps moving in that direction.
sentences.zh: 一旦你开始了这个过程，系统就会沿着这个方向不断发展。

sentences.en: Like a point of no return.
sentences.zh: 就像不归路一样。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, if we're already seeing signs that this current is weakening, does that mean we're possibly already past that point of no return?
sentences.zh: 那么，如果我们已经看到这股洋流正在减弱的迹象，这是否意味着我们可能已经走过了那条不归路？

sentences.en: is it no longer a matter of if, but when?
sentences.zh: 这已经不再是“是否会发生”而是“何时发生”的问题了吗？

sentences.en: The really short answer is we just don't know.
sentences.zh: 最简单的回答是：我们根本不知道。

sentences.en: The best guess is that it's not going to shut down this century.
sentences.zh: 最好的猜测是它不会在本世纪停转。

sentences.en: But plenty of scientists are worried.
sentences.zh: 但许多科学家都很担忧。

sentences.en: It's something that a lot of them are focused on very intensely just because we do think the consequences if AMOC did shut down could be so catastrophic.
sentences.zh: 这是许多人高度关注的焦点，因为我们确实认为，如果 AMOC 真的停转，其后果可能是灾难性的。

sentences.en: If that current collapsed though, like, is there anything we could do to bring it back?
sentences.zh: 然而，如果洋流崩溃了，我们有什么办法能让它恢复吗？

sentences.en: Like, it did come back
sentences.zh: 它在

sentences.en: 13,000 years ago after that last ice age.
sentences.zh: 上一次冰河时代之后的 13,000 年前确实恢复过。

sentences.en: What happened?
sentences.zh: 当时发生了什么？

sentences.en: Short answer again, nobody is quite sure.
sentences.zh: 简而言之，谁也不太确定。

sentences.en: It seems to have abruptly grown warm again over 40,
sentences.zh: 在经历40到

sentences.en: 50 years, but it's pretty unclear why.
sentences.zh: 50 年后，它似乎又突然变暖了，但原因很不明确。

sentences.en: And I think as far as what would happen today to bring it back,
sentences.zh: 我认为，至于今天要采取什么措施才能让它恢复，

sentences.en: scientists, would still say cutting greenhouse gas emissions and preventing the planet from overheating is probably the only thing we have in our control that could influence
sentences.zh: 科学家们仍然会说，减少温室气体排放、防止地球过热，可能是我们唯一能掌控的、能够影响

sentences.en: the climate on that scale.
sentences.zh: 这种规模气候的手段。

sentences.en: I mean, it's sort of where we land at the end of every episode about climate change.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这差不多是我们每集讨论气候变化节目结束时的归宿。

sentences.en: And it's sort of interesting, I mean, probably like a lot of people listening to you, I find all this pretty scary and dystopian and worrying.
sentences.zh: 而且挺有意思的，我是说，可能和许多听你节目录音的人一样，我觉得这一切都挺可怕、反乌托邦而且令人担忧。

sentences.en: It's kind of crazy to think actually that scientists have warned about this for decades.
sentences.zh: 回想起来其实挺疯狂的，科学家几十年前就已经发出过警告。

sentences.en: That there was even a science fiction movie made 20 years ago, which, you know, in some ways predicted what might be the real consequences of this current shutting down.
sentences.zh: 甚至在20年前还拍过一部科幻电影，你知道的，它在某些方面预测了当前这种停摆可能带来的真实后果。

sentences.en: It's not like we humans lack the imagination of like all the terrible things we're risking here.
sentences.zh: 这并不是说我们人类缺乏想象力，想象不到我们在这里冒着风险的种种可怕后果。

sentences.en: But when it comes to protecting ourselves and the planet against this existential threat, we are clearly unwilling to do what it takes.
sentences.zh: 但当我们要保护自己和地球免受这种生存威胁时，我们显然不愿意付出代价。

sentences.en: scientists have been thinking about AMOC and had a pretty good grasp of what AMOC looked like decades ago.
sentences.zh: 科学家们一直在思考大西洋经向翻转环流（AMOC），并且在几十年前就对它的样貌有了相当不错的掌握。

sentences.en: As early as the 80s and
sentences.zh: 早在80年代和

sentences.en: 90s, scientists made this connection between the warming that humans were bringing about and consequences like an AMOC collapse and other things as well.
sentences.zh: 90年代，科学家们就将人类带来的变暖与AMOC崩溃等后果联系在了一起。

sentences.en: It was one of the scientists who wrote about AMOC in the 80s who said the climate system is an angry beast and we are poking it with sticks.
sentences.zh: 正是当年在80年代撰写过关于AMOC文章的一位科学家说过，气候系统是一头愤怒的野兽，而我们正在用棍子去戳它。

sentences.en: And that's still true today.
sentences.zh: 直到今天，这句话依然适用。

sentences.en: Well, Raymond, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 好的，雷蒙德，非常感谢。

sentences.en: Thank you,
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，

sentences.en: Katrin.
sentences.zh: 卡特琳。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.zh: 特朗普，他最不想做的事情就是把他送进监狱。

sentences.en: But at the end of the day, he had a job to do and would seriously consider it.
sentences.zh: 但归根结底，他有自己的职责要履行，并会认真考虑这一点。

sentences.zh: 该提议由埃及和卡塔尔的调解员提出，但以色列回应称，该提议未能满足其要求。

sentences.en: The prime minister's office said it would still send a delegation to talk about how to reach an acceptable deal.
sentences.zh: 总理办公室表示，仍将派遣代表团就如何达成一项可接受的协议进行会谈。
